title: Metabolic-State Crossover: Allostatic Threshold Modulation Under Energy Deficit
description: Four-session, two-site crossover compares fasting/fed and vigilance/rested states for selective interoceptive impairment beyond arousal; the two depletion modalities remain distinct.

sub_predictions.claim: Metabolic depletion selectively elevates θₜ for high-interoceptive-load stimuli, reducing d′ disproportionately compared to neutral exteroceptive stimuli.
sub_predictions.confirming_evidence: State x Load interaction on d-prime: p <0.0167, BF10 >=100 and eta_p_squared >=0.06; signed depletion contrast delta_dprime_extero - delta_dprime_intero >=0.15 * rested_intero_dprime, where delta=depleted-rested and rested_intero_dprime must be positive.
sub_predictions.falsifying_evidence: (a) No significant Metabolic State × Interoceptive Load interaction classified as Scenario E (p ≥ 0.05 AND BF₀₁ ≥ 6) on d′ or P3b amplitude; OR (b) metabolic depletion produces a uniform, global suppression of ignition proxies across all stimulus types, indicating generalized cognitive fatigue rather than selective θₜ elevation.
sub_predictions.indeterminate_rule: Failure to confirm alone is not evidence of falsification. Apply the registered interval/evidence rule and admissibility gate.
sub_predictions.source: OSF Table 19, supplemented by detailed protocol decision rules below.
sub_predictions.signed_margin: delta_dprime_extero - delta_dprime_intero >= 0.15 * rested_intero_dprime; delta=depleted-rested; baseline must be positive.
sub_predictions.nonpositive_baseline_rule: Zero or negative rested interoceptive d-prime is inadmissible for the proportional margin; report only the separate absolute-scale secondary contrast >=0.15 d-prime units.

sub_predictions.claim: The neural ignition proxy (P3b amplitude) reflects selective θₜ elevation: P3b is disproportionately suppressed for detected high-interoceptive-load stimuli under metabolic depletion.
sub_predictions.confirming_evidence: Significant Metabolic State × Interoceptive Load interaction on P3b amplitude (p < 0.0167); P3b reduction for interoceptive targets exceeds exteroceptive targets by ≥ 1.5 µV after arousal covariation.
sub_predictions.falsifying_evidence: Uniform P3b suppression across all stimulus types; or P3b interaction disappears after covarying for pupil diameter / HRV (indicating an arousal confound rather than allostatic triage).

primary_hypothesis: Depletion reduces interoceptive d-prime and P3b more than exteroceptive measures; the signed interactions survive pupil/RMSSD adjustment.
primary_analysis: Pred 4.A: seen ~ Signal * MetabolicState * InteroceptiveLoad + Modality + Site + (1 + Signal * MetabolicState | Participant), probit GLMM. apgi_parameters.model: Reduced empirical specification: seven core quantities plus somatic modulation; not eight freely fitted parameters in every dataset.

gamma_sig.role: population-fixed model sigmoid steepness; distinct from alpha_psy

beta_SM.role: somatic modulation gain; not independently identifiable from Pi_i using behavior alone

kappa.role: energy-information bridge only; never ignition steepness

apgi_parameters.gain_interpretation: Pi_i in the reduced confirmatory model is salience-weighted gain; HEP is a candidate indicator, not a direct inverse-variance measurement.
apgi_parameters.accumulation: S_next=(1-a_S)*S+a_S*u; a_S=1-exp(-dt/tau_S); u uses calibration-fixed relative gains and excess magnitudes abs(z)-sqrt(2/pi).
apgi_parameters.ignition: p_k=1-exp(-r_max*sigmoid(gamma_sig*(S-theta))*dt); single trial-window sigmoid sampling is a distinct convention, never interchanged within a protocol.
apgi_parameters.time_step: dt=0.01 s reduced reference; dt<=min(tau_S,tau_theta,tau_Pi)/10; active reservoir additionally requires dt<=tau_res/10.
apgi_parameters.parameter_manifest_status: Required before confirmatory fitting; no unspecified coefficient is assigned a legacy default.

quality_and_decision_rules.data_admissibility: Apply registered quality gates before inference. Inadmissible data are exploratory, receive no Scenario A–F, and carry no framework vote.

scenarios.A: Scenario A — Confirmed. p < α and BF₁₀ ≥ 100. Both streams converge on H₁. Counted toward framework-level BY-FDR confirmation and toward the joint Bayesian meta-analysis. No additional replication is required before the claim is filed.
scenarios.B: Scenario B — Tentative confirmation. p < α and 3 ≤ BF₁₀ < 100. The frequentist threshold is met but Bayesian evidence is moderate rather than strong; reported as "frequentist-significant, Bayesian moderate." One pre-registered independent replication is required before the result is elevated to confirmatory status, and that replication is registered before the primary result is published.
scenarios.C: Scenario C — Discordant (frequentist-positive, Bayesian-null). p < α and BF₁₀ < 3. The frequentist threshold is met but the Bayes factor provides less than moderate evidence for H₁ and may favor H₀. Classified as equivocal: the result neither confirms nor falsifies the prediction. It is flagged as equivocal in the results and recorded in the analysis log (not in the protocol-deviation register, which is reserved for departures from registered procedure). Independent replication at ≥ 90% power is required before any interpretation is made.
scenarios.D: Scenario D — Bayesian positive (without frequentist significance). p ≥ α and BF₁₀ ≥ 100. Strong probabilistic support for H₁ while the NHST threshold is missed. Not counted toward BY-FDR (which operates on the frequentist p-values). The original study plus one pre-registered replication are required for elevation to confirmatory status.
scenarios.E: Scenario E — Bayesian falsification. p ≥ α and BF₀₁ ≥ 6. The frequentist result is nonsignificant and the Bayesian analysis supports H₀. Classified as provisional falsification of the specific sub-prediction and reported as such in the primary manuscript. A single Scenario E result triggers independent replication at ≥ 90% power before the sub-prediction is declared definitively falsified, and triggers review of whether the framework-level falsification threshold has been reached (two or more Scenario E results across primary protocols; framework-level decision rule).
scenarios.F: Scenario F — Indeterminate. p ≥ α and 1/6 < BF₁₀ < 100 (i.e., neither BF₁₀ ≥ 100 nor BF₀₁ ≥ 6). Neither stream reaches a decision threshold. Classified as inconclusive: it carries no confirmatory or falsifying weight and is reported transparently as indeterminate. It may motivate a pre-registered replication but does not by itself trigger one, and it is never counted toward BY-FDR confirmation or framework-level falsification.

quality_and_decision_rules.framework_confirmation: At least 4/5 primary protocols, combined hierarchical BF10>=100, and at most one Scenario E protocol. Protocol 0 is a gate; 2 contributes F2; 6 is CE.
quality_and_decision_rules.protocol_alpha_specification: Protocol 4 (Metabolic-State Crossover): Bonferroni α = 0.0167 across the three primary models (Pred 4.A d′, Pred 4.B P3b, Pred 4.C covariate-adjusted); BF₁₀ ≥ 100 required for strong confirmation; minimum effect size ηₚ² ≥ 0.06. Falsification threshold: the interaction is absorbed by arousal covariates (reduction Δηₚ² ≥ 0.02) or meets Scenario E (p ≥ 0.05 and BF₀₁ ≥ 6) after covariate entry.
quality_and_decision_rules.decision_precedence: Prediction-specific estimands, interval/evidence rules and admissibility gates govern over abbreviated source summaries. The A–F matrix applies only where both frequentist and Bayesian hypotheses are explicitly defined; do not invent a point-null Bayes factor. Nonsignificance or a point estimate alone does not establish equivalence or falsification; specificity requires a direct contrast. Unresolved interval bounds or multiplicity allocations require prospective analysis lock.

submission_blocking_issues: Level-2 mechanistic timescale model/recovery simulation not specified; ordering deferred, session trends descriptive.
Threshold-recovery analysis remains exploratory; no primary framework falsification vote.

specification_sections.heading: Metabolic State Modulates Allostatic Thresholds
specification_sections.text: Protocol 4 (Metabolic-State Crossover) is designed to test for the computational claim that the ignition threshold (θₜ) is dynamically regulated by metabolic state as an allostatic triage mechanism. Under conditions of energy deficit, the framework predicts that the brain selectively elevates θₜ to suppress high-cost interoceptive channels while preserving essential exteroceptive processing. This prediction must be reconciled with Pred 2.B, in which homeostatic threat prioritizes interoceptive ignition. The registered resolution is that fasting and prolonged vigilance impose a resource deficit without an acute homeostatic threat signal, so the cost term (c_θ·Cₜ) dominates and costly interoceptive channels are deprioritized, whereas acute threat (Protocol 2 environments) raises V_info for interoceptive errors. If Protocol 4 shows interoceptive prioritization under depletion, the cost-dominance assumption — not the threshold equation — is falsified. The fasting arm manipulates metabolic state directly; the vigilance arm manipulates sustained cognitive load as a resource-depletion proxy, and the two arms are analyzed as distinct modalities.

specification_sections.heading: Experimental Design
specification_sections.text:
A pre-registered, arousal-covaried, within-subject crossover design is employed across two independent laboratories (N = 64 enrolled / N = 55 analyzable, minimum N = 48; powered at 0.80 to detect the critical interaction at d = 0.45 with α = 0.0167, accounting for 15% attrition and multi-site variance).

Each participant completes four sessions (fasted, fed, vigilance-depleted, rested) in counterbalanced order with ≥ 48 h between sessions; modality order is counterbalanced within each laboratory, never across laboratories, so that modality is not confounded with site.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Comparison Conditions and Induction Modalities
specification_sections.text:
Metabolic depletion is induced via two validated, counterbalanced modalities to prevent modality-specific confounds:

Fasting Arm: 16-hour overnight fast vs. fed control state (standardized 600 kcal meal 2 hours prior; capillary glucose confirmed ≥ 4.5 mmol/L at session onset).

Vigilance Arm: Prolonged time-on-task vigilance paradigm (4-hour continuous AX-CPT) vs. rested baseline.

Within each metabolic state, participants detect two interleaved stimulus streams: high-interoceptive-load stimuli (visual targets synchronized to the systolic cardiac phase, or threat-conditioned cues) and neutral exteroceptive stimuli (synchronized to diastole, or unconditioned neutral cues).

Level-2 ordering falsification target. The three-timescale ordering τ_int,ℓ > τ_ign,ℓ > τ_θ,ℓ (H10; Multi-Scale paper) is most testable at Level 2, where the three constants separate by orders of magnitude. Standard EEG/psychophysics operates at Level 1, where they collapse toward equality. The Protocol 4 sustained-vigilance arm (4-hour continuous AX-CPT) is therefore the committed Level-2 falsification target for the ordering. Three quantities are estimated across the vigilance decrement and tested for the predicted ordering:

τ_int,2 — evidence-accumulation slowing, indexed by the decline in drift rate v from a hierarchical drift-diffusion model fit to AX-CPT responses in successive 30-minute bins.

τ_ign,2 — broadcast-maintenance change, indexed by P3b duration (full width at half maximum of the 250–500 ms parietal component) across the same bins.

τ_θ,2 — refractory recovery, indexed by post-response detection-threshold rebound measured by interleaved near-threshold probes.

The 30-minute-bin trajectories estimate session-scale change parameters, not τ_int, τ_ign or τ_θ by an exponential fit alone. An ordering test on those mechanistic constants requires the archived generative state and observation equations connecting within-bin probes to each parameter, with recovery and uncertainty simulations. Until that model is specified and validated, the session trends are descriptive and the mechanistic ordering is deferred. Confirming evidence: the posterior probability of the joint ordering τ_int,2 > τ_ign,2 > τ_θ,2 exceeds 0.95. Falsifying evidence: the posterior probability of the ordering is below 0.05, i.e. the predicted ordering is positively disfavored. Where a Level-2 estimate is unavailable for any of the three constants — through insufficient vigilance decrement, model non-convergence, or probe attrition — the ordering prediction is explicitly labeled "deferred — Level 2" and is not treated as tested at Level 1. Consistent with H10's "Speculative" register status, this test can confirm or defer but cannot serve as a primary framework refuter.

specification_sections.heading: Pre-requisite Dependency
specification_sections.text: Protocol 4 has a partial dependency on Protocol 0 (HEP Proxy Validation). Pred 4.A (d′) and Pred 4.B (P3b) do not invoke HEP as a primary measured variable and remain confirmatory regardless of Protocol 0 outcome. The Protocol 0 dependency activates only for any Protocol 4 secondary analysis that includes HEP amplitude as a covariate or mediator; those analyses are automatically reclassified as exploratory if Protocol 0 fails.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Task Environments
specification_sections.text: Near-Threshold Detection Task: Participants perform a visual detection task using Gabor patches or conditioned cues. A 50-trial pre-session adaptive QUEST staircase (50% detection criterion) establishes each participant's individual threshold c₅₀. The main session presents stimuli at c₅₀ ± one geometric step (0.71, 1.0, 1.41 × c₅₀), ≥ 80 trials per level, plus 25% blank catch trials. Stimuli are strictly synchronized to cardiac phases to manipulate interoceptive load.

specification_sections.heading: Methodological Rigor and Safety Protocols
specification_sections.text:
Artifact Gating: Continuous online monitoring (technician alert at ±200 µV); offline rejection at 150 µV peak-to-peak (§4.2.1). A session with > 30% trial rejection fails the Data-Admissibility Gate.

Physiological Monitoring: Continuous pupillometry and HRV (RMSSD) recorded to dissociate allostatic metabolic effects from general LC-NE arousal.

Safety: The fasting arm screens for metabolic contraindications (diabetes, eating disorders); sessions terminate if symptomatic hypoglycaemia (glucose < 3.5 mmol/L) or presyncope occurs. The vigilance arm terminates if HRV drops > 40% from baseline concurrent with subjective distress.

specification_sections.heading: Pred 4.A — Selective Behavioral Threshold Elevation
specification_sections.text: Metabolic depletion selectively elevates θₜ for high-interoceptive-load stimuli, reducing d′ disproportionately relative to neutral exteroceptive stimuli. Confirming: significant Metabolic State × Interoceptive Load interaction on d′ (trial-level probit GLMM, p < 0.0167, ηₚ² ≥ 0.06), with the depletion-induced reduction in d′ for interoceptive-load stimuli exceeding that for exteroceptive stimuli by ≥ 15% of the participant's baseline interoceptive d′ (with Δd′ = depleted − rested, the signed contrast Δd′_exteroceptive − Δd′_interoceptive ≥ 0.15 × d′_interoceptive,rested for participants with positive rested interoceptive d′). Participants with zero or negative rested interoceptive d′ are inadmissible for this proportional margin and enter only a separately reported absolute-scale secondary contrast (Δd′_exteroceptive − Δd′_interoceptive ≥ 0.15 d′ units). An absolute difference without its sign cannot confirm selective interoceptive impairment.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Pred 4.B — Selective Neural Ignition Suppression
specification_sections.text: P3b amplitude (250–500 ms), the neural ignition proxy, reflects selective θₜ elevation. P3b is disproportionately suppressed for detected high-interoceptive-load stimuli under metabolic depletion. Confirming: significant Metabolic State × Interoceptive Load interaction on P3b amplitude (p < 0.0167, BF₁₀ ≥ 100), with P3b reduction for interoceptive targets exceeding exteroceptive targets by ≥ 1.5 µV after arousal covariation.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Pred 4.C — Metabolic Specificity (Arousal Dissociation)
specification_sections.text: The allostatic triage effect is predicted to survive adjustment for arousal markers; this does not by itself establish mediation by metabolic cost. Confirming: the Metabolic State × Interoceptive Load interaction on both d′ and P3b remains significant when trial-level baseline pupil diameter and RMSSD are included as nuisance covariates (Δηₚ² < 0.02 reduction in the interaction term).

specification_sections.heading: Falsification Criteria
specification_sections.text:
No Interaction: No significant Metabolic State × Interoceptive Load interaction on d′ or P3b amplitude, classified as Scenario E (frequentist p ≥ 0.05 AND BF₀₁ ≥ 6) in the primary LMM.

Uniform Suppression: Metabolic depletion produces a global suppression of ignition proxies across all stimulus types, indicating generalized cognitive fatigue or LC-NE arousal rather than selective θₜ elevation.

Arousal Confound: The interaction effect is fully absorbed by arousal covariates (Δηₚ² ≥ 0.02 loss, or the interaction meets Scenario E — p ≥ 0.05 AND BF₀₁ ≥ 6 — after covariation), indicating the effect is driven by general arousal rather than metabolic allostatic triage.

Threshold time-constant bounds. Following ignition-inducing events, θₜ is predicted to show rapid decrease (τ ≈ 200–500 ms) during surprise accumulation and slow recovery (τ ≈ 10–30 s) following sustained activation. If rapid threshold recovery (τ_θ < 3 s) is observed, or if threshold shows no decay within 60 s (τ_θ > 60 s), in ≥ 60% of participants (N ≥ 60, exact binomial, α = 0.05), the allostatic timescale claim is falsified and APGI's allostatic threshold dynamics require fundamental revision. Deviations within 2–5× of the predicted values (e.g. τ_θ = 5 s or 50 s) necessitate parameter refinement but not framework rejection. The τ_θ recovery analysis is exploratory under the current register and contributes no primary falsification vote. Rapid recovery (< 3 s) and absence of identifiable decay within 60 s are exploratory refinement outcomes, with their uncertainty reported. Any upgrade requires a pre-collection amendment fixing the boundaries, observation model and final analyzable-N/power requirement; otherwise an imprecise or unavailable estimate is deferred.

τ_θ is estimated by the Bayesian state-space model of §4.2.3 from interleaved near-threshold probes in the vigilance arm. This timescale test is not in the confirmatory register (Tables 12 and 15) and is reported as exploratory unless added by amendment before Protocol 4 data collection.

specification_sections.heading: Statistical Analysis
specification_sections.text:
Analysis uses Linear Mixed-Effects Models (LMM) fitted via the lme4 package in R, with the following pre-registered model specifications:

Pred 4.A (unadjusted) d′ model, trial-level probit GLMM: seen ~ Signal × MetabolicState × InteroceptiveLoad + Modality + Site + (1 + Signal × MetabolicState | Participant); the Signal × MetabolicState × InteroceptiveLoad coefficient is the d′ interaction (DeCarlo, 1998). Pred 4.C (adjusted): the same model plus trial-level PupilDiameter and session-level RMSSD

P3b model (Pred 4.B, unadjusted): P3b_Amplitude ~ MetabolicState × InteroceptiveLoad + Modality + Site + (1 + MetabolicState | Participant). Pred 4.C (adjusted): the same model plus trial-level PupilDiameter and session-level RMSSD.

The critical test in both models is the interaction term. Confirmation requires p < 0.0167 and BF₁₀ ≥ 100 for that term; ηₚ² ≥ 0.06 is the minimum effect size requirement. Heterogeneous results across the fasting and vigilance modalities trigger a pre-specified modality-stratified secondary analysis with random-effects aggregation.

methods_source_sections.heading: Outliers and influence
methods_source_sections.text:
4.3.2 Outlier and influential-observation policy

All rules below are fixed pre-collection and apply to every protocol unless a protocol body specifies otherwise; no post-hoc outlier rule may be introduced. (a) Trial level. Scalp-EEG trials exceeding the 150 µV peak-to-peak criterion (§4.2.1) are rejected; iEEG trials follow the interictal-discharge and |z| > 6 rule of §Protocol 6; behavioral trials in speeded detection tasks with RT < 150 ms or > 3 s are rejected as anticipations or lapses (Protocol 2 IGT and Protocol 7 bedside tasks use the rules in their protocol bodies). No further trial-level trimming is permitted. (b) Participant level. A participant is excluded only for a pre-registered admissibility failure (> 30% trial rejection, Data-Admissibility Gate; failed manipulation check; protocol violation). Statistical outlyingness is never itself an exclusion ground. (c) Observation level in models. Continuous predictors and outcomes are winsorized at ±3 SD within participant before entry into any confirmatory model; the untrimmed analysis is reported alongside as a mandatory sensitivity analysis, and a discrepancy in the confirmatory decision between the two is reported as an instability flag. (d) Influence. For every confirmatory regression or mixed model, Cook's distance is computed and observations with D > 4/n are reported; the model is refit without them as a sensitivity analysis. The trimmed refit is never the confirmatory result. (e) Model diagnostics and fallback. Gaussian models use the registered residual diagnostics; binary/ordinal generalized models use distribution-appropriate simulation or predictive diagnostics, not a Shapiro–Wilk residual gate. Appendix C must identify the exact estimator, tuning constants, inferential test and Bayesian evidence computation for each permitted fallback before lock. A fallback not so specified is a sensitivity analysis and cannot replace the primary confirmatory estimator.

methods_source_sections.heading: Bayesian prior sensitivity
methods_source_sections.text:
Sensitivity analyses

All confirmatory Bayesian conclusions are re-run under fixed prior transformations. Normal and HalfNormal priors: scale multiplied by 2 and by ½, location and support unchanged. Beta(2, 5) prior on η_RL: mean (2/7) preserved and concentration (sum of shape parameters, 7) multiplied by 2 and by ½, giving Beta(4, 10) and Beta(1, 2.5). Fixed parameters remain fixed or vary over a separately registered grid. Every evidence and interval criterion is recomputed under each sensitivity prior; if a conclusion crosses a §3.5.2 decision boundary (BF₁₀ = 3 or 100, BF₀₁ = 6), it is reported as prior-sensitive and reclassified as exploratory.

methods_source_sections.heading: Scalp EEG acquisition
methods_source_sections.text:
4.1.1 Scalp EEG (Protocols 0, 1, 4, 5, 7)

EEG will be acquired at 1000 Hz (TMS-EEG in Protocol 5: ≥ 5000 Hz on a TMS-compatible amplifier) using a 64-channel active electrode system (BrainProducts actiCHamp or equivalent). Electrode positions will be digitized using 3D photogrammetry (EGI Geodesic or equivalent). Online reference (all protocols): single physical reference at FCz (or the amplifier's default), with A1/A2 or TP9/TP10 recorded as separate channels. Post-acquisition re-referencing (all protocols): average reference after RANSAC bad-channel interpolation (correlation threshold < 0.85 with neighbors). Sites using mastoid-referenced amplifiers must apply offline average-reference conversion before any cross-protocol pooling. The acquisition target is impedance < 10 kΩ. For 10–20 kΩ, the technician attempts correction and records the affected electrodes; data remain admissible only if the registered signal-quality and bad-channel criteria pass. Impedance > 20 kΩ invokes the registered corrective/admissibility procedure. Impedance alone does not override the trial-quality gate.

ECG will be simultaneously recorded for HEP analysis (Lead II configuration). Skin conductance (SCR/EDA) will be acquired at 100 Hz from the thenar and hypothenar eminences of the non-dominant hand. Respiration will be recorded via respiratory inductance plethysmography or nasal thermistor (§4.2.1). All auxiliary channels will be synchronized with EEG via trigger pulses with sub-millisecond accuracy.

Heartbeat-evoked potential (HEP) analysis: epochs from −200 to +600 ms relative to the R-peak will be extracted after artifact rejection; the HEP analysis window is 250–400 ms post-R-peak (Appendix A). Ectopic beats are excluded when the R-R interval deviates by > 20% from the median of the five preceding intervals, and R-R intervals outside 500–1500 ms (40–120 bpm) are excluded. Exclusion counts are reported per condition, and differential exclusion between the drug and placebo arms of Protocol 0 is tested. HEP amplitude will be quantified as mean amplitude in the 250–400 ms window over frontocentral electrodes (Fz, FCz, Cz).

methods_source_sections.heading: EEG preprocessing and mandatory HEP controls
methods_source_sections.text:
4.2.1 EEG Pre-Processing

EEG preprocessing will follow the PREP pipeline (Bigdely-Shamlo et al., 2015) supplemented by custom APGI-specific steps:

Re-reference to average reference (all electrodes except those flagged as bad) after RANSAC bad channel interpolation (threshold: correlation < 0.85 with neighboring channels). This is the binding cross-protocol standard; protocol-specific mastoid references noted in companion documents are superseded for all pooled analyses.
Bandpass filter: 0.1–100 Hz (zero-phase FIR, Hamming window); notch filter at the local mains frequency (50 or 60 Hz) and harmonics. The 0.1–100 Hz pipeline applies to standard ERP analyses only. Infraslow/PAC analyses use a separately frozen branch: DC-coupled (or hardware high-pass ≤ 0.005 Hz) acquisition, a 0.005–100 Hz zero-phase FIR passband, continuous segments of ≥ 30 min for Pred 7.E (≥ 500 s for the MS-H1 infraslow test; §Spectral Fitting Parameters), and removal of the first and last 60 s of each segment to exclude filter transients. Frequencies removed by acquisition or filtering are not reconstructed; a dataset not meeting the DC/≤ 0.005 Hz requirement has its infraslow test deferred
Independent Component Analysis (ICA): extended Infomax (MNE-Python); components classified using ICLabel (threshold: eye artifact > 0.80, muscle artifact > 0.80, reject)
HEP-specific artifact control (binding for all HEP measurement in Protocols 0, 1, 4, 5 and 7). The following supersede the generic ICLabel step for any analysis in which HEP amplitude is a dependent or independent variable, and are mandatory rather than advisory.
Cardiac field artifact — three-stage removal pipeline, applied in sequence. (a) ICA decomposition with cardiac component identification via template matching to simultaneously recorded ECG; a correlation of r > 0.80 with the ECG template is required for rejection. (b) Residual artifact inspection via visual review of the grand-average HEP time-locked to the QRS peak; any deflection exceeding ±2 µV in the 0–80 ms window indicates insufficient cardiac removal and triggers a second ICA pass. (c) HEP analysis restricted to the 250–400 ms post-R-peak window, which lies outside the QRS complex but overlaps the T-wave / cardiac field artifact (CFA, peaking ≈ 300 ms post-R); a surrogate-R-peak control (HEP recomputed on R-peaks shuffled within the participant's R-R distribution) and an ECG-amplitude covariate are confirmatory conjuncts: a primary HEP effect is confirmed only if it exceeds the surrogate distribution (permutation p < α) and survives the ECG covariate. The later window (455–595 ms) is reported as a robustness check. The 250–400 ms window is canonical; deviation requires explicit justification and artifact-check documentation filed as a protocol amendment.
Respiratory phase. Continuous respiratory monitoring via respiratory inductance plethysmography or nasal thermistor throughout all HEP recording sessions. Any trial in which the R-peak falls within 100 ms of a respiratory peak or trough — defined as the extrema of the bandpass-filtered (0.1–0.5 Hz) respiratory signal — is excluded from HEP analysis. Respiratory phase is additionally included as a nuisance covariate in all HEP general linear models, and reported HEP effects must survive this covariate. If the respiratory covariate absorbs more than 30% of the HEP variance in the primary contrast (partial η² > 0.30), the result is flagged as potentially confounded and reported with a confound-warning label pending replication under paced breathing.
Arousal. Pupil diameter (baseline-corrected, 200–500 ms post-R-peak) is recorded on all trials via high-speed eyetracking (≥ 500 Hz, constant luminance). Any primary HEP–P3b association is reported both uncorrected and as a partial correlation controlling for trial-level pupil diameter; see Pred 1.D for the binding thresholds.
Non-compliance. An analysis that omits any stage of this pipeline is automatically exploratory under §3.5.3 and carries no framework-level weight.
Epoch extraction: −200 to +1000 ms relative to stimulus onset; baseline correction −200 to 0 ms
Artifact rejection: trial-level peak-to-peak amplitude threshold of 150 µV (series-canonical): a trial is rejected when max(x) − min(x) > 150 µV within the analysis epoch on any scalp channel; peak-to-peak amplitudes are nonnegative; the ±200 µV online monitor threshold is a technician alert, not a rejection criterion; linear detrending; muscle artifact detection via high-frequency power (> 3 SD from mean)
Participants with > 30% rejected trials fail the registered admissibility gate. Report enrolled, excluded and analyzable counts separately. Replacement recruitment is permitted only within the protocol’s preregistered enrollment cap and stopping rules; exceeding that cap requires an amendment before additional recruitment. Excluded participants remain in the recruitment and adverse-event accounting.

methods_source_sections.text:
Protocol 4 (Metabolic-State Crossover)

Status: Ethics approval pending at time of registration lock.
Committee: Protocol is registered as a planned study and the registration will be amended with committee name, institution, approval number and date before any participant is approached.
16-hour fasting protocol: Medical clearance required; contraindicated for diabetes, hypoglycemia history, metabolic disorders, eating disorders and pregnancy. Capillary glucose and β-hydroxybutyrate are measured at session onset and end as the metabolic manipulation check.
4-hour vigilance task: Fatigue monitoring with the termination rule in §Protocol 4 (RMSSD drop > 40% with distress ≥ 6/10, Borg CR10). Terminated sessions are retained and analyzed with time-to-termination as a covariate, because termination is informative.
